absences.searched: Bourse 1933 (Grève des autobus - Place de la Bourse, le public attendant la reprise, Peyriras 1933; Commons page https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gr%C3%A8ve_des_autobus_-_Place_de_la_Bourse,_le_public_attendant_la_reprise_-_btv1b90350369.jpg)
absences.result: extmetadata LicenseShortName 'Public domain', but its only rationale is 'PD France' (agency work, 1933). No US rationale is tagged, and a 1933 French photograph not PD in France on 1 Jan 1996 would have had its US copyright restored (URAA) to 2029. So it is not verifiably PD everywhere. It was REPLACED by Agence Rol 1919 plates (PD-1996, published before 1931). commons/bourse1933.jpg (local sha1 6410b220ff1f39cacf027edd912d2ec648167372, Commons original sha1 6bdbbb7760906432fe72d6a023e7042d7b8d4c41) is not used; raw metadata in evidence/bourse-meta.json

absences.searched: Moving Image Archive cache: clips with audio.kind sound matching street|traffic|bus|tram|car|engine|bell|crowd|paris (28 hits; spectrograms of 545715d8 Water 1953, 14c8b94b Third Avenue El, d2ed8576 Look to Lockheed 1940, 9970bcd5 Inside the Fed 1994)
absences.result: none usable: Water, Lockheed and Inside the Fed carry narration or music in the window (formant/harmonic bands); Third Avenue El is a steady broadband hiss band with no street events; rights for the 1990s titles are not PD. Commons was used instead.

absences.searched: Commons audio: 'tram bell', 'bus engine', 'street traffic', 'bicycle bell', 'old bus idling', 'city street ambience' (filetype:audio)
absences.result: no recording of a pre-1930 motorbus engine or of a period omnibus conductor bell under an allowed licence; a 1991 diesel bus engine (CC BY) and a bicycle bell (CC0) are used and declared. WWS Firedepartmentbell (CC BY 4.0, a 19th-century fire-engine bell) was a candidate but its download was rate-limited (HTTP 429) and it is not needed.

absences.searched: Commons crowd plates 1910s-1920s (Agence Rol/Meurisse): foule autobus Agence Rol; Rol foule Paris; foule Rol 1919
absences.result: no 1910s-20s Rol/Meurisse plate of a crowd at a bus stop; the Vilgrain queue (1919) gives full-length walkers on clear ground, which cut cleanly
